adds.rationale: Swapping in a defense prime captures the structural NATO/European rearmament buildup (Zeitenwende, Madrid summit spending pledges) that the profile names, replacing an AI holding whose near-term fundamentals just deteriorated.

news_evidence.summary: Lockheed Martin Q2 2022 ending backlog of $134.6B, ~36% expected to convert to revenue over the next 12 months.
NATO leaders at Madrid summit agree to hike military spending; ~$350B cumulative increase in European/Canadian defense spending since 2014 by end of 2022.

removes.rationale: Two dated material hits this quarter (gaming demand collapse and a new China AI-chip export ban) mark a thesis breach the tight 3-slot cap can no longer absorb next to a stronger geopolitical/defense candidate.

news_evidence.summary: Nvidia Q2 FY23 gaming revenue $2.04B, down 44% sequentially and 33% YoY, citing weak sell-through and macro headwinds.
New US export restrictions bar Nvidia's advanced A100/H100-class AI chips to China/Hong Kong; up to $400M Q3 sales at risk.

rationale_overall: The watchlist stays at its 3-slot cap: NVDA exits on two dated quarter-specific hits (44% sequential gaming drop; new China AI-chip export ban into its highest-growth segment), and Lockheed Martin enters to capture the NATO/European rearmament buildup (Madrid pledges, Germany's Zeitenwende fund, Lockheed's record backlog). MSFT and GOOGL kept; no comparable dated thesis breach surfaced for either. Net: one AI slot rotates into geopolitical/defense. Nuclear names (Cameco/Westinghouse) traced to October 2022 decisions and were excluded to avoid leakage.
